repos.brief:
**What it does:** An open-source Chinese-authored book (with 13 language translations) covering AI Agent design and engineering across 10 chapters, paired with 95 runnable experiments spanning RAG, MCP, multi-agent systems, context engineering, and reinforcement learning.

**Why now:** The repo gained 7,406 stars this week alone, signaling a surge in developer interest likely tied to the simultaneous release of PDF/EPUB builds in 13 languages — making the full text newly accessible to non-Chinese readers via community translations into English, Russian, Japanese, and others.

**Build with it:** Clone the repo, run the chapter-specific Python experiments under the MCP or multi-agent sections, and use them as scaffold code to wire your own tool-calling agent against a local or API-hosted LLM — the 95 labs give you a concrete starting point rather than blank-page architecture decisions.

**What it does:** OmniRoute is a self-hostable TypeScript gateway that routes requests across 290+ AI providers through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with quota-aware fallback and RTK+Caveman token compression that can cut prompt size by 15–95%.

**Why now:** The repo gained 6,561 stars this week, signaling a surge of developers actively hitting rate limits across Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor as those tools see heavier daily use — making multi-provider fallback practically urgent rather than optional.

**Build with it:** Point your existing `OPENAI_BASE_URL` in Claude Code or Cursor to the OmniRoute endpoint, configure a fallback chain across Gemini Flash, GPT-4o mini, and Kimi free tiers, and let the quota-aware router handle limit exhaustion without changing your client code.

**What it does:** A structured 21-lesson curriculum from Microsoft covering generative AI fundamentals through hands-on Jupyter Notebooks, spanning prompt engineering, RAG, fine-tuning, image generation with DALL-E, and LLM application deployment.

**Why now:** The repo gained 2,480 stars this week, coinciding with sustained developer interest in agentic AI workflows — Lesson 17 covers AI agents specifically, making it a timely on-ramp as teams evaluate frameworks like AutoGen and Semantic Kernel for production agent builds.

**Build with it:** Fork the repo and run the agent or RAG lessons locally against Azure OpenAI or the OpenAI API by dropping credentials into the provided `.env` setup, then extend the Semantic Kernel notebook in Lesson 17 to wire a custom tool-calling agent into your own data source.

**What it does:** Agent Reach is a Python CLI that routes AI agents to read and search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, and XiaoHongShu without paid API keys, using multi-backend fallback so platform-side blocks swap silently (e.g., yt-dlp → bili-cli when Bilibili's rate limiting hit in June 2026).

**Why now:** The repo hit GitHub's #1 trending repository of the day this week with 4,910 stars added, surfacing at the moment Claude Code and Cursor adoption is pushing builders to extend agents beyond local context into live web data.

**Build with it:** Drop `agent-reach doctor` into your Claude Code or Cursor workflow as a pre-flight step, then wire the MCP search backend and per-platform cookie config via `agent-reach` CLI commands to give any LLM agent scoped, structured access to live social and video content without touching each platform's auth layer yourself.

**What it does:** Ponytail is a Claude Code skill/agent plugin that injects a "laziest senior dev" heuristic into AI coding agents, steering them toward minimal implementations (e.g., `<input type="date">` instead of installing flatpickr) and measurably reducing generated code by ~54% on average across real feature tasks.

**Why now:** The repo is trending at nearly 5,000 stars this week, coinciding with the broader Claude Code plugin/skill ecosystem maturing as a concrete extension surface — builders are actively mapping what agent behavior shaping looks like in practice.

**Build with it:** Drop the skill into your Claude Code config via `@dietrichgebert/ponytail` on npm, then run it against any feature branch to audit over-built PRs before merge — the `git diff` output becomes your LOC/cost benchmark, comparable against the project's own agentic benchmark methodology in `benchmarks/`.

**What it does:** Graphify parses any codebase—plus its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs—into a queryable knowledge graph using deterministic tree-sitter AST analysis, with every edge explained and no vector store required.

**Why now:** The project is trending at +4,710 stars this week, coinciding with active adoption across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI as developers standardize on MCP-based skill workflows for code navigation.

**Build with it:** Add a `/graphify` skill to your Claude Code or Cursor setup, then query cross-file call graphs and schema relationships directly from your AI assistant's chat interface instead of writing bespoke grep pipelines or embeddings infrastructure.

**What it does:** CC Switch is a Tauri-based desktop app that centralizes configuration and provider switching for CLI AI coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok Build, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent — from a single GUI.

**Why now:** Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter open model with a 1M-token context window, launched this week and is already a featured sponsor integration, giving it immediate relevance as a routing target for teams evaluating frontier coding models.

**Build with it:** Drop CC Switch into a multi-agent dev workflow to manage `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, base URL overrides, and skill profiles per tool from one config surface — useful if you're benchmarking Kimi K3 against Claude Sonnet across Codex and OpenCode without editing dotfiles per session.

**What it does:** AirLLM runs large language models — up to 671B (DeepSeek-V3) and 2.8T (Kimi K3) parameters — on consumer GPUs with as little as 4GB VRAM by streaming individual model layers or MoE experts from disk rather than loading the full model into memory.

**Why now:** The Kimi K3 (2.8T) support landed in July 2026, making it the largest open-source model runnable on a single card; with 3,903 new stars this week, builders are actively evaluating it as local-inference hardware access widens.

**Build with it:** Drop in `AutoModel` from `airllm`, point it at a Hugging Face model ID, and run 4-bit or 8-bit quantized inference on a local GPU inside an existing `transformers`-compatible pipeline — no architecture changes required beyond `pip install airllm compressed-tensors flash-attn`.

**What it does:** TencentDB Agent Memory is a self-hosted memory layer for AI agent teams that extracts four typed assets — Chat Memory, Skills, LLM-Wiki, and Code-Graph — from conversations, documents, and code, then makes them queryable and shareable across agents and sessions.

**Why now:** The repo jumped 3,738 stars this week, coinciding with growing friction around context-window costs and session amnesia as teams scale multi-agent workflows beyond single-session prototypes.

**Build with it:** Drop it into a Claude Code or CodeBuddy setup via the included proxy and `start-all.sh`, then configure your agent to call the MCP-compatible Memory Hub at `localhost:8125` so Skills and Code-Graph entries accumulated in one session are automatically available to the next agent that picks up the task.

**What it does:** Hermes Agent is a self-improving Python agent from Nous Research that creates and refines skills from experience, maintains persistent memory across sessions, and runs on any LLM backend (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, local endpoints) across CLI, Telegram, Discord, and cloud execution environments including Modal and Daytona.

**Why now:** The project is pulling 3,567 stars this week, placing it among the fastest-moving agent repos currently — coinciding with broad builder interest in alternatives to Claude Code and Codex that aren't locked to a single model provider or local machine.

**Build with it:** Point it at your own OpenRouter or Nous Portal endpoint via `hermes model`, then wire a Telegram gateway to a Modal serverless backend so the agent hibernates between tasks — you get a persistent, model-agnostic coding or automation assistant that costs nothing when idle and wakes on incoming messages.
